blocks.x: Pierre Sage endured a frustrating return to Lyon in the Europa League as his Crystal Palace side lost 3-2 to his former employers at the Groupama Stadium.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half without a shot on target for the visitors. Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s two-goal advantage. The Palace substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find an equaliser.

Days after beating his predecessor, the Nottingham Forest manager, Oliver Glasner, at Selhurst Park in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage found himself returning to the home of the club he managed for 14 months.
Ismaïla Sarr, who claimed the Conference League golden boot last season, was in the Crystal Palace starting lineup for the first time this season.

Celtic found a clinical Benfica side too much to handle during a 4-1 defeat in Lisbon. The Colombia striker Jhon Durán scored for the hosts with a penalty after just five minutes having been fouled by Dane Murray and completed his double in the 35th minute, after the defender Alexander Bah had doubled Benfica’s lead earlier in the half.

Martin O’Neill’s side were cut apart at times but could have scored themselves on a couple of occasions before the break. The visitors eventually reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute through a brave header from Camilo Durán – who had joined up with the squad late after remaining in Glasgow for the birth of his second child – but they could not close the gap any further before the substitute Vangelis Pavlidis fired in a fourth for the home side with two minutes remaining.

Georginio Rutter got Brighton’s campaign off to a flying start and sent a message to his manager, Fabian Hürzeler. Rutter has lost his place to Charalampos Kostoulas and was making his first start since the opening day of the season against the Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris.

Randal Kolo Muani scored a stoppage-time header to give Juventus a 2-1 win at Celta Vigo which leaves them top of the standings. Hugo Álvarez had put the home side in front early on before Nick Woltemade equalised on the hour and Kolo Muani then nodded in from close range during the second minute of added time.

Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at RB Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick by the Italian teenager Alphadjo Cissè. Milan’s record signing Gonçalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the shine off the win for Ruben Amorim’s side.
